questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
The fact that I got to have the proper college experience which did not fail! UT Austin is a lot like you see on the movies, in a very good way! You get too meet so many new people from all over the world, whilst also experiencing texas. Even though Austin is very democratic you can still get a feel for the proper texan lifestyle. 
The academics was honestly very good too, way more practical than what is was used to back home which I really liked.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There are multiple lectures and welcome meetings to prepare you for the following semester (they usually start 1,5 weeks before the actual semester starts and the rest of the UT students arrive at campus).

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was easy. I lived at a CO-OP (collegehouses) it by far the cheapest option (985 dollars per month) and the rent includes food. You will however need to do approx 4. Hours of labor for the house each week which can for example be cooking. Make sure to plan you labor (if you choose this option) in the weekdays as you will want your weekends free. CO-OPs are also a great way to meet americans and other exchange students. It is however not luxurious in any way! and you do not have much privacy if you opt for a double room. Other options are apartments with other exchange students from your own country, this is also a very good option but a lot more expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It seemed easier to find housing off campus than on campus

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You will get a date and a time where the registration is opened to all exchange/international students, and it is first come first serve. Make sure to write down all the courses you want and their unique number beforehand in excel so you can copy paste easily so you get the courses you want. Also make sure you have gotten approval from your study counsellor for the courses you want beforehand or it will not let you register for the course (this might change depending on major)

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer:
For my major I had a virtual meeting with a study counsellor from that major, here I told him which courses I would like to do and he “pre-approved” me for those courses. 
Make sure to get the pre approval for all the courses you might take even your second choices as some courses might get filled up fast. (Note that not all courses need pre-approval, but check it in advance).

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all my courses in the end. At first I did not get one of my courses but I signed up for the waiting list for the course, and during drop week (a week where you can try and change courses as much as you want, enough people dropped the course and I was admitted).

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do research on the courses beforehand, download UT registration plus (chrome plugin), and talk to a study counsellor.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I did mostly upper level undergraduate courses, it is pretty hard to get approval for graduate courses. The workload is a bit bigger than back home (granted I also did an extra course), but every single assignment during the semester will likely count toward your final grade so you cannot just slack for half the semester.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Mostly lectures, but much smaller classes with room for questions. Also some group work, but be aware that Americans (at least in my experience, and other exchange students’ experience) are quite bad a doing group work so if the final product matters to you, you might need to take on a leadership role early in the process.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was not that bad if you buy it and make it yourself from HEB or Walmart.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are so many clubs/orgs that are absolutely awesome! They will all have stalls on speedway the first couple of weeks of fall semester, go talk to them and figure out what you like.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join the wakeboard club it is an incredible experience! You will get to go on a boat every other week and wakeboard/wakesurf, you will meet great people and likely also attend some great parties/formals.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Travel around the US, go to football games, ask local families to join them for holidays if you can befriend some.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, people are very accommodating!

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just talk to people, they are pretty open. Go to parties. Join a club/org. (People usually have back to back classes so they have to hurry, therefore it is pretty hard to socialise in the classrooms).

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing really, only the fact that you can’t address the professors by their first name.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
The unity around all the college sports (especially american football, which is only in the fall semester)
The fact that people actually wear boots and hats, and not as a costume
The fact the everything is so over the top compared to Denmark, in a very good way. 
The openness of people

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be open to experience, and talk to as many people as you can, you won’t regret it. 

It will be very expensive no matter how you do it so make sure to save/apply for scholarships ahead of time so you won’t have to worry too much about financials. 

All the issues you have beforehand will likely resolve themselves, and it is way easier to solve them once you are actually In texas.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You get so much free stuff with your UT (E)ID. NY times, Public transport, Amazon prime, Uber one, Canva. Use it.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The Unity around campus, especially regarding the college sports. The new friends. Experiencing Texas and US culture first hand.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Balancing having fun/experiencing things and academic work.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
